column3: “Any man” renders “a man, a man,” and “shall surely be put to death” renders an emphatic doubled verb (throughout the chapter).
“My holy name” renders “the name of my holiness.”
“should ever disregard” renders an emphatic doubled verb, “hiding they hide their eyes.”
“his family” renders “his clan,” and “play the harlot” renders “prostitute themselves after.”
“anyone” renders “a man, a man”; “or” renders “and,” and “his bloodguiltiness” renders “his bloods” (throughout the chapter).
“a disgrace” renders “hesed,” a word that usually means lovingkindness but here means shame; “his guilt” renders “his iniquity.”
NASB supplies “such a one”; “his blood relative” renders “his kin (she’er).”
“ordinances” renders “judgments,” and “spew you out” renders “vomit you up.”
